root_idea.summary: A root oriented toward impairment, corruption, or disorder, especially affecting bodily members and faculties.
root_idea.development: The core notion of bodily فساد extends to mental derangement, damaged or disordered affairs, loss, destruction, distress, and related figurative uses. The lending and livestock-management terms are treated as a divergent lexical branch.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Quran-attested nominal form with a distinct lexical entry.

senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic occurrences, خبال denotes corruption or harmful disorder brought about in people's affairs, rather than the broader Classical senses of mental derangement, bodily impairment, or literal destruction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become corrupt, unsound, vitiated, or disordered; hence, to become mentally deranged or insane.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Also used of a limb or member that becomes impaired, immobile, dried up, lost, or cut off.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be afflicted with paralysis.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The cited term for the paralysis is فَالِج.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To render someone mentally deranged or to corrupt, impair, or disorder his reason, heart, or limb.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The subject may be grief, love, time, fortune, disease, or another cause; the construction may describe deprivation of reason or impairment of a member.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To restrain, withhold, debar, prevent, or hinder someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Commonly followed by عَنْ with the thing from which someone is prevented.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To fall short of performing or matching an action.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested in the expression خَبَلَ عَنْ فِعْلِ أَبِيهِ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The lending of an animal for use, such as riding, obtaining milk, or travel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Especially used of lending a she-camel, horse, camels, or sheep and goats.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Dividing one's camels into two groups so that each group breeds in alternate years.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A livestock-management practice compared with alternating cultivation of land.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a beast, to cease remaining in its customary place.
To seek to corrupt, impair, or disorder some of another person's camels.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The object is livestock in the cited construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To ask for or seek a loan, especially of livestock; a loan or a demand for a loan.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The cited livestock construction concerns borrowing an animal or herd until a time of abundance; the broader nominal use is reported of anything.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Corruption, unsoundness, or disabling disorder of the limbs or members.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Includes impairment of a person's limbs or of a beast's legs, inability to walk, and the paralysis termed فَالِج.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The cutting off or loss of arms, hands, legs, or feet.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural خُبُول is attested in claims involving blood and severed limbs.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A wound, or wounds for which compensation or redress is claimed.
Trial, punishment, slaughter, civil conflict, discord, or dissension.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative or extended use equated with فِتْنَة and هَرْج.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An addition paid beyond what a camel-owner or attendant imposes by stipulation.
An incoming thought or idea.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested in the idiom وَقَعَ فِي خُبْلِي, comparable to “it came into my mind.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: Jinn or genii; also a devil.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Some authorities also apply the term to mankind; the plural and quasi-plural usage varies in the lexical reports.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A bird said to cry throughout the night with a single repeated cry.
A leather water-bag or waterskin, especially a full one.
Corrupted, unsound, disordered, or mentally deranged; of a person, also lacking heart or having impaired extremities; of a beast, impaired in the legs.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjective covering mental and bodily impairment, including a condition likened to amputated extremities.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Difficult or unhappy, said of a time or period.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use for a time in which its people see no happiness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Corruption resulting from a wound.
A corrupt, unsound, vitiated, or disordered state in actions, bodies, or minds; including mental derangement, foolishness, heedlessness, or weakness of intellect.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This broader Classical sense includes an affection resembling possession or insanity and is distinct from the specifically Quranic use of خبال for corruption or harmful disorder in affairs.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Loss or diminution.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A derived or extended sense equated with نُقْصَان.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Perdition, destruction, wasting away, or being consumed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Describes a thing's going, passing, or wasting away.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The hollow-sided, deteriorated condition of an old well.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The hollow may catch and lacerate a bucket as it enters.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Fatigue, weariness, distress, embarrassment, affliction, trouble, or difficulty.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: May describe a person who is a source of hardship or trouble to his family.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A deadly poison.
The fluid squeezed or flowing from the inhabitants of Hell or from their skins.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested in the expression طِينَةُ الْخَبَال.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Corrupting, rendering unsound, vitiating, or disordering, especially the reason or intellect.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The form may be used intensively with the corresponding impairment term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A proper name for Time.
The legs of a beast.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare reported usage whose correctness is explicitly questioned in the lexical evidence.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Pointer-only cross-reference to the Form I entry.
The separately named palsy is included in the bodily-impairment meaning.
The general loan and demand-for-loan use is grouped with the livestock loan construction.
The application to mankind is included as a qualification of the jinn/devil meaning.
The full waterskin is included under the leather water-bag meaning.
Intensive usage is stated in the target usage conditions.

cautions: The reported meaning مُخْتَبِلُ دَابَّةٍ “the legs of a beast” is explicitly treated as doubtful in the lexical evidence.
